newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar up on shortage of stock, low buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar up on shortage of stock, low buying.

text.p: Sugar prices climbed up on the local market on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Fresh consumer buying however remained low due to the conclusion of holy festival (festival of colours) but negligible arrivals and a shortage of ready stock dragged prices upward," one dealer said.
In ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 7/30 rupees to 1,262/1,300 rupees per quintal while M-30 climbed by 15/35 rupees to 1,305/1,380 rupees per quintal.
Sugar mill delivery bounced back to 1,190/1,210 rupees from 1,170/1,180 rupees per quintal.

"Major transport operators in India plan to go on indefinite strike next month and against this backdrop leading traders recently demanded to relax time schedule for lifting sugar from the mills," one broker said.
"But the millers refused this demand and now traders have started lifting lower quantity from the mills which has created a shortage of sugar in the Bombay market," he added.
Indian transporters plan an indefinite strike to protest the levy of a new service tax and a hike in insurance premiums.
